newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO CONTRACT TALKS HIT SNAG OVER BONUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO CONTRACT TALKS HIT SNAG OVER BONUS.

text.p: A dispute over a 2.0 billion peseta ($14 million) bonus hit talks to keep Brazilian striker Ronaldo at Barcelona, Spanish media said on Wednesday.

Reports said negotiations had been suspended over different views about the one-off bonus agreed last October. The Spanish club reportedly said it would pay it to ensure Ronaldo did not go to another team.

Barcelona wanted to pay the money through a company based in the Virgin Islands to save on taxes estimated at 1.0 billion pesetas ($7 million). But Ronaldo's agents demanded the money be paid in Spain net of taxes.
A spokesman for Barcelona said he had no comment on the reports.
The club said on Tuesday Ronaldo had renewed his 10-year contract with the Catalan team.

The 20-year-old striker signed on for nine more years at 500 million pesetas ($3.5 million) a season after protracted talks on the cost of breaking his contract, which was finally set at 10 billion pesetas ($69.9 million).

Barcelona had been holding out for 15 billion pesetas ($104.85 million), almost double the amount clubs have to pay to poach other star players from Spain and almost treble the four billion ($27.98 million) set when Ronaldo first signed the contract in 1996.
Italian, English and French clubs had shown interest in Ronaldo, whose 34 goals this season are far more than any other player in the Spanish league or the European Golden Boot competition.
